route.text: Liouville's denominator argument on the set G: if G sums to p/q then, for every m in G, q·L·(tail of G from m) is a positive integer, where L is any common multiple of the 2^a - 1 over a in G below m, while the tail is below 4·2^(-m); so 2^m < 4q·L at every element m of G. This closes the hole for every G that is eventually lacunary of ratio two (proved in full: variant-d144ccc1, with the criterion variant-1629563f) and for nothing denser.

literature_proposed.summary: Open. Given --h1 (a representation of a rational is the greedy one), this hole is equivalent to the root: it says the greedy representation of every rational is finite. Known cases of the root (A = ℕ, eventually periodic A, pairwise coprime A with Σ1/a < ∞, squarefree numbers, perfect powers, primes) each show only that particular A is not the greedy representation of a rational; none controls the greedy walk of a given rational.

import Mathlib

theorem witness : ∃ (r : ℚ) (G : Set ℕ),
  (0 : ℕ) ∉ G ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ),
        (1 : ℕ) ≤ n →
          (n ∈ G ↔
            (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ n - (1 : ℝ)) ≤
              (↑r : ℝ) - ∑' (a : (↑(G ∩ Set.Iio n) : Type)), (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (↑a : ℕ) - (1 : ℝ)))) ∧
      ∑' (n : (↑G : Type)), (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (↑n : ℕ) - (1 : ℝ)) = (↑r : ℝ) := by
  refine ⟨0, ∅, Set.notMem_empty 0, ?_, by rw [tsum_empty]; simp⟩
  intro n hn
  have h2 : (2 : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ n := by
    calc (2 : ℝ) = 2 ^ 1 := by norm_num
      _ ≤ 2 ^ n := pow_le_pow_right₀ (by norm_num) hn
  have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ n - 1) := by
    apply div_pos one_pos; linarith
  haveI : IsEmpty (↑((∅ : Set ℕ) ∩ Set.Iio n) : Type) := ⟨fun x => x.2.1⟩
  rw [tsum_empty]
  simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, false_iff, not_le]
  simpa using hpos
